evidence.label: Absolutely Continuous Spectrum for Weak-Disorder Anderson Models in Dimensions at Least Three
Pure-Point Spectrum for the Two-Dimensional Anderson Model at Every Positive Disorder

headline: Claims electrons stay trapped on a random square grid at any disorder, and can spread at weak disorder in 3D.
scope: The nearest-neighbour Anderson model with independent uniform random potentials: the square lattice at every disorder, and dimensions three and up at weak disorder.
plain: The Anderson model describes an electron hopping on a grid where each site has a random energy. Physicists expect that in two dimensions any amount of randomness traps the electron, while in three dimensions weak randomness lets it spread on some energies. Two papers claim to prove both pictures for uniform random energies. Lean proves only that the allowed energies on the square grid fill the interval from −4 − h to 4 + h.
doesNot: This does not prove exponential decay of eigenfunctions, dynamical localization, the location of the mobility edge, or quantum diffusion.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Philip W. Anderson, random site energies as a mechanism that suppresses quantum transport
scorecard.significanceWhy: Planar localization at weak disorder and absolutely continuous spectrum in three dimensions are listed open problems from Simon's 2000 problem list.

explanation:
Picture an electron on a square grid, like a sheet of graph paper. At each step it can hop to one of its 4 neighbours. Each site x also has a random energy v_x, drawn uniformly between −h and h. The number h is the disorder strength. Without randomness, a wave spreading evenly across the grid has energy 2cos k₁ + 2cos k₂ for some wave numbers k₁ and k₂. Those values fill the interval from −4 to 4. Random energies widen this to −4 − h up to 4 + h. For h = 0.5 the allowed energies, called the spectrum, run from −4.5 to 4.5.

The question is whether the electron spreads or stays put. Anderson introduced random site energies as a way to suppress quantum transport[1]. In maths language, staying put means pure-point spectrum: the grid has a full set of trapped wave shapes, called eigenvectors. Spreading means absolutely continuous spectrum, with no trapped states at those energies. A physical scaling theory predicts no true metal in two dimensions[2]. So in the plane, any disorder h > 0 should trap the electron.

Earlier proofs worked only for strong disorder or for energies near the edges. Fröhlich, Martinelli, Scoppola and Spencer showed pure-point spectrum in those regimes[3]. Edge results remain restricted to a bottom interval of energies[4]. Weak disorder in the middle of the band is the hard case. There the randomness is a small push, and it must still beat the wave's tendency to spread.

The second paper claims the planar case. For each h > 0, almost surely the square-grid operator has pure-point spectrum and a complete basis of eigenvectors[5]. The paper says this resolves the pure-point part of the two-dimensional Anderson localization conjecture for uniform energies[6]. It does not claim exponential decay or dynamical localization[7].

The first paper goes the other way, in dimension 3 and higher. There Simon's Problem 1 asks for an energy range with purely absolutely continuous spectrum[8]. The paper claims such a range for small disorder: on a fixed open interval of energies, the spectrum is purely absolutely continuous[9]. On a tree-shaped lattice, the Bethe lattice, Klein proved this decades earlier[10]. In three dimensions the interval sits just above the bottom edge −6 of the free band. The paper does not locate the full mobility edge, the energy where spreading switches to trapping[11].

How sure is this? Lean, a computer proof checker, proves one supporting fact. On the square grid, the spectrum is almost surely the interval from −4 − h to 4 + h. The trapping and spreading claims are outside Lean. They rest on two long papers, and no specialist review of them has been published.
hypeCheck: Major if it holds. Lean proves only the spectral interval on the square grid. The trapping and spreading claims rest on two long papers with no published specialist review.

glossary.meaning: An electron hopping between neighbouring grid sites, where each site has its own random energy.
The width of the random energies: each site's energy is uniform between −h and h.
The set of energies the electron can have in this model.
The case where trapped wave shapes (eigenvectors) span everything; it means the electron stays localized.
Energies with no trapped states, where waves spread out, like in a metal.
With probability one over the random choice of site energies.
An energy where behaviour switches from spreading to trapped.
